sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- kb_show_binding: Show this repo's knowledge-base binding
- kb_list_projects: List available knowledge-base projects
- kb_list_documents: List documents in the bound knowledge-base project
- kb_get_document: Fetch a knowledge-base document by slug or id
- kb_upsert_document: Save a decision, summary, or note to the knowledge base
- kb_backlinks: Find notes that link TO a slug
- kb_resolve_links: Resolve outbound links from a note
- vcc_recall: vcc_recall: Search history; default scope is active lineage. Use scope:'all' for off-lineage branches. Use scope:'compaction:N' or scope:'compaction:latest' for targeted search within a compaction segment. expand:[indices] returns full content for those entries, composable with query to expand matched results.
- subagents_enable: pi-subagents is installed. For authorized specialist, independent-review, or parallel work, call subagents_enable, then subagent. Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- If kb_show_binding reports no project is bound, ask the user to run /ada:bind before any other knowledge-base operation.
- Use kb_list_projects to discover knowledge-base projects when the repo is not bound or the user references one by name.
- Use kb_list_documents to enumerate notes in the bound project when the user asks what has been recorded or you need to find a slug.
- Use kb_get_document to read an existing note by slug or id before answering questions grounded in the knowledge base.
- Use kb_upsert_document to save a decision, summary, or note to the knowledge base. Provide a slug, a title (required when creating), and markdown content that may use [[slug]] wikilinks to other notes.
- Use kb_backlinks before renaming or deleting a note to see which other notes link to it via [[slug]], and to confirm the target exists.
- Use kb_resolve_links to show what a note links to and confirm those targets exist; dangling [[slug]] links are flagged, not errors.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: kb_show_binding
toolsAdded.description: Show which Ada AI knowledge-base project this repository is bound to, by reading .pi/kb-binding.json (no network). Call this first to learn which project knowledge-base operations target, and to detect when the repo is not bound.

toolsAdded.name: kb_list_projects
toolsAdded.description: List the Ada AI knowledge-base projects available to the current session (id and name for each). Use when the repo is not bound and you need to suggest a project, or when the user asks what knowledge bases exist.

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_list_documents
toolsAdded.description: List documents in a knowledge-base project as metadata (id, slug, title, updated) — bodies are NOT included and there is no full-text search in v1, so call kb_get_document to read a specific note. Uses the repo binding unless project_id is given.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_get_document
toolsAdded.description: Fetch one knowledge-base document WITH its markdown content, by slug (unique within a project) or numeric id. Use to read a note the user references or one found by kb_list_documents or a link graph.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_upsert_document
toolsAdded.description: Create or update a knowledge-base note by slug. Creates when the slug is new (title required) and updates the existing document in place when it exists (omitted fields are left unchanged server-side). Content may use [[slug]] wikilinks to other notes in the same project.

slug.description: Note slug: 1-80 lowercase [a-z0-9-], not starting or ending with '-'.

title.description: Note title. Required when creating; left unchanged on update when omitted.

content.description: Markdown body. May contain [[slug]] wikilinks. Omit on update to leave unchanged. Capped at 1 MB.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_backlinks
toolsAdded.description: Compute which documents in a knowledge-base project reference a slug via [[slug]] wikilinks, and whether the target document itself exists. The server does not compute backlinks, so this scans all documents in the project. Use before renaming or deleting a note, or to understand its impact.

slug.description: Target slug to find backlinks for.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_resolve_links
toolsAdded.description: Resolve one hop of outbound [[slug]] links from a note, fetching each target. Dangling links (target document does not exist) are flagged, not treated as errors. Use to show what a note links to and verify its targets.

slug.description: Slug of the note to resolve outbound links from.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: vcc_recall
toolsAdded.description: Search session history. Defaults to active lineage; use scope:'all' to include off-lineage branches. Supports regex queries, paging, and expand indices. Use scope:'compaction:N' to search within a specific compaction's message range.

query.description: Search terms or regex pattern (e.g. 'hook|inject', 'fail.*build'). Multi-word = OR ranked by relevance.

expand.description: Entry indices to return full untruncated content for. Works alone (any index in scope) or alongside query (expands matching entries on the current page).

page.description: Page number (1-based) for paginated search results. Default: 1.

scope.description: Search scope. Options: 'lineage' (default), 'all' (entire session), 'compaction:N' (within compaction #N), 'compaction:latest' (most recent compaction segment).

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background, provider, or detached work that has no native completion notification, then return.

Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively when they complete or need attention. In an interactive chat, return control instead of calling this merely to wait. Use this tool for provider jobs, remembered detached foreground runs, or other background work without a native notification path. Headless runs auto-drain current-session subagent work at agent_end; use this tool only when the current turn must receive non-notifying background work results.

• { } — return when the first initially active async run or registered provider item finishes, or when a subagent needs attention.
• { all: true } — wait for every async run, provider item, and remembered detached foreground descendant that was active when the call began.
• { id: "..." } — wait for one async or remembered detached foreground subagent run (id or prefix). Named async runs that already finished return their terminal result references.
• { id: "...", nonBlocking: true } — resolve the prefix once, persist an exact-run wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this for detached work without native completion delivery; the originating interactive session wakes on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout.
• { stopOnAttention: false } — for blocking waits only, keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.
• { timeoutMs: 600000 } — stop waiting after N ms; active work keeps running. Omitted values use waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 minutes. Window expiry returns a non-error window_elapsed result with active work identities.

Non-blocking subscriptions are visible in subagent status and differ from disabling waitTool: waitTool.enabled=false returns immediately without registering any future wake. Provider jobs are session-scoped and identified exactly, so replacing one job with another cannot hide a completion. Provider extensions must be explicitly loaded in this process. In a child agent, keep `bg_wait` in the child tool allowlist and load each provider through the agent's extensions or subagentOnlyExtensions; this tool never loads providers or grants tools itself.

id.description: Async run or remembered detached foreground run id/prefix to wait for one specific run. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use bg_wait for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, or when same-turn blocking results are truly needed. Omit to wait across every active async run started in this session only when a same-turn wait is truly needed.

nonBlocking.description: When true, resolve id to one exact run, persist a wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this only for provider, detached, or other background work without a native completion notification; ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively and do not need a subscription. The originating session is woken on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout. Requires id and cannot be combined with all.

all.description: Wait for ALL active runs to finish. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use all only when a same-turn result from tracked background work is truly needed. Default false: return when the first tracked run or provider item finishes or needs attention. Ignored when id targets a single run.

timeoutMs.description: Give up waiting after this many milliseconds (the runs keep going regardless). Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use a wait timeout only when same-turn results are truly needed for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification. Defaults to config waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 1800000 (30 minutes). Window expiry is a non-error active-work result.

stopOnAttention.description: For a blocking wait that is truly needed, stop when a run needs attention by default. Set false to keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.

toolsAdded.name: subagents_enable
toolsAdded.description: Enable pi-subagents delegation and management tools without launching work. Call when delegation is authorized by the current request or applicable user/project instructions, or when managing existing runs. Direct execution is the default; complexity alone never authorizes delegation. Full tools are available on the next model request.

toolsAdded.name: goal_complete
toolsAdded.description: Mark an active /goal complete only when the latest effective Goal contract explicitly says Goal mode is active, supplies the matching current goal_id, and every requirement is verified. Tool visibility alone does not activate Goal mode. Never call for ordinary work, partial progress, blockers, failures, or unverified work.

goal_id.description: The exact goal_id shown in the current active /goal prompt. Used only to reject stale completion calls from older turns.

summary.description: State what was completed and what evidence verified it. Do not use this tool to report partial progress, blockers, failures, or remaining work.

toolsAdded.name: goal_blocked
toolsAdded.description: Stop an active /goal only when the latest effective Goal contract explicitly says Goal mode is active, supplies the matching current goal_id, and the same evidenced external blocker recurred for at least three consecutive Goal turns. Tool visibility alone does not activate Goal mode. Never call for ordinary clarification, uncertainty, incomplete work, or recoverable failures.

goal_id.description: The exact goal_id shown in the current active /goal prompt.

reason.description: The specific user or external action required to unblock the goal.

evidence.description: Concrete evidence from the repeated attempts that proves the impasse.

arguments.command: for n in 105 106 112 113 114 115 116; do gh pr view $n --json number,state,headRefName,mergeCommit --jq '"\(.number) \(.state) \(.headRefName) \(.mergeCommit.oid)"' 2>&1; done

cmp_delta() {  # $1=branch $2=pr-merge-commit(or empty)
  b=$1; mc=$2
  base=$(git merge-base origin/main $b)
  d1=$(git diff $base $b | git patch-id --stable | cut -d' ' -f1)
  if [ -n "$mc" ] && git cat-file -e $mc 2>/dev/null; then
    d2=$(git diff ${mc}^ $mc | git patch-id --stable | cut -d' ' -f1)
    after=$(git rev-list --count $mc..$b)
    [ "$d1" = "$d2" ] && verdict="delta==PR-squash (fully merged)" || verdict="delta DIFFERS from PR squash; commits-after-merge=$after"
  else
    verdict="no merge commit given"
  fi
  echo "$b: $verdict"
}

#   recall     -- AC2: run KDA_RECALL_PROBE against a live serve.
#   bench      -- AC4: compare measured bench JSON vs the 638514 baseline.

sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- kb_show_binding: Show this repo's knowledge-base binding
- kb_list_projects: List available knowledge-base projects
- kb_list_documents: List documents in the bound knowledge-base project
- kb_get_document: Fetch a knowledge-base document by slug or id
- kb_upsert_document: Save a decision, summary, or note to the knowledge base
- kb_backlinks: Find notes that link TO a slug
- kb_resolve_links: Resolve outbound links from a note
- vcc_recall: vcc_recall: Search history; default scope is active lineage. Use scope:'all' for off-lineage branches. Use scope:'compaction:N' or scope:'compaction:latest' for targeted search within a compaction segment. expand:[indices] returns full content for those entries, composable with query to expand matched results.
- subagents_enable: pi-subagents is installed. For authorized specialist, independent-review, or parallel work, call subagents_enable, then subagent. Authorization must come from the current request or applicable instructions; complexity alone is not authorization.

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- If kb_show_binding reports no project is bound, ask the user to run /ada:bind before any other knowledge-base operation.
- Use kb_list_projects to discover knowledge-base projects when the repo is not bound or the user references one by name.
- Use kb_list_documents to enumerate notes in the bound project when the user asks what has been recorded or you need to find a slug.
- Use kb_get_document to read an existing note by slug or id before answering questions grounded in the knowledge base.
- Use kb_upsert_document to save a decision, summary, or note to the knowledge base. Provide a slug, a title (required when creating), and markdown content that may use [[slug]] wikilinks to other notes.
- Use kb_backlinks before renaming or deleting a note to see which other notes link to it via [[slug]], and to confirm the target exists.
- Use kb_resolve_links to show what a note links to and confirm those targets exist; dangling [[slug]] links are flagged, not errors.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background, provider, or detached work that has no native completion notification, then return.

Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively when they complete or need attention. In an interactive chat, return control instead of calling this merely to wait. Use this tool for provider jobs, remembered detached foreground runs, or other background work without a native notification path. Headless runs auto-drain current-session subagent work at agent_end; use this tool only when the current turn must receive non-notifying background work results.

• { } — return when the first initially active async run or registered provider item finishes, or when a subagent needs attention.
• { all: true } — wait for every async run, provider item, and remembered detached foreground descendant that was active when the call began.
• { id: "..." } — wait for one async or remembered detached foreground subagent run (id or prefix). Named async runs that already finished return their terminal result references.
• { id: "...", nonBlocking: true } — resolve the prefix once, persist an exact-run wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this for detached work without native completion delivery; the originating interactive session wakes on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout.
• { stopOnAttention: false } — for blocking waits only, keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.
• { timeoutMs: 600000 } — stop waiting after N ms; active work keeps running. Omitted values use waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 minutes. Window expiry returns a non-error window_elapsed result with active work identities.

Non-blocking subscriptions are visible in subagent status and differ from disabling waitTool: waitTool.enabled=false returns immediately without registering any future wake. Provider jobs are session-scoped and identified exactly, so replacing one job with another cannot hide a completion. Provider extensions must be explicitly loaded in this process. In a child agent, keep `bg_wait` in the child tool allowlist and load each provider through the agent's extensions or subagentOnlyExtensions; this tool never loads providers or grants tools itself.

id.description: Async run or remembered detached foreground run id/prefix to wait for one specific run. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use bg_wait for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, or when same-turn blocking results are truly needed. Omit to wait across every active async run started in this session only when a same-turn wait is truly needed.

nonBlocking.description: When true, resolve id to one exact run, persist a wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this only for provider, detached, or other background work without a native completion notification; ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively and do not need a subscription. The originating session is woken on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout. Requires id and cannot be combined with all.

all.description: Wait for ALL active runs to finish. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use all only when a same-turn result from tracked background work is truly needed. Default false: return when the first tracked run or provider item finishes or needs attention. Ignored when id targets a single run.

timeoutMs.description: Give up waiting after this many milliseconds (the runs keep going regardless). Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use a wait timeout only when same-turn results are truly needed for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification. Defaults to config waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 1800000 (30 minutes). Window expiry is a non-error active-work result.

stopOnAttention.description: For a blocking wait that is truly needed, stop when a run needs attention by default. Set false to keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.

toolsAdded.name: subagents_enable
toolsAdded.description: Enable pi-subagents delegation and management tools without launching work. Call when delegation is authorized by the current request or applicable user/project instructions, or when managing existing runs. Direct execution is the default; complexity alone never authorizes delegation. Full tools are available on the next model request.

toolsAdded.name: goal_complete
toolsAdded.description: Mark an active /goal complete only when the latest effective Goal contract explicitly says Goal mode is active, supplies the matching current goal_id, and every requirement is verified. Tool visibility alone does not activate Goal mode. Never call for ordinary work, partial progress, blockers, failures, or unverified work.

goal_id.description: The exact goal_id shown in the current active /goal prompt. Used only to reject stale completion calls from older turns.

summary.description: State what was completed and what evidence verified it. Do not use this tool to report partial progress, blockers, failures, or remaining work.

toolsAdded.name: goal_blocked
toolsAdded.description: Stop an active /goal only when the latest effective Goal contract explicitly says Goal mode is active, supplies the matching current goal_id, and the same evidenced external blocker recurred for at least three consecutive Goal turns. Tool visibility alone does not activate Goal mode. Never call for ordinary clarification, uncertainty, incomplete work, or recoverable failures.

goal_id.description: The exact goal_id shown in the current active /goal prompt.

reason.description: The specific user or external action required to unblock the goal.

evidence.description: Concrete evidence from the repeated attempts that proves the impasse.

repeated_turns.description: Number of separate turns spent trying to resolve this same blocker.

toolsAdded.name: goal_wait
toolsAdded.description: Keep an active /goal quiet only when the latest effective Goal contract explicitly says Goal mode is active, supplies the matching current goal_id, and progress depends on an arranged external wake event or one safety deadline. Tool visibility alone does not activate Goal mode. Call goal_wait alone. Requests below 10000ms are clamped to 10000ms. Never call for ordinary unfinished work.

goal_id.description: The exact goal_id shown in the current active /goal prompt.

reason.description: Why the goal is waiting and which external event should wake it.

resume_after_ms.description: Optional safety deadline in milliseconds that requests one continuation if no wake message arrives. Values below 10000 are accepted but clamped to 10000.

3c76e4a perf(kda): warp-per-row float4 layer_norm_gated — 174 -> 4.8 us on MI300A (35x, issue #144)
The one-thread-per-row layout launched N/256 = 32 blocks on MI300A's 228
CUs (occupancy-bound, 72 GB/s = 1.4% of HBM). Rewrite as one warp per
token row: 256-thread block handles 8 rows (N/8 = 1024 blocks), lane l
holds elements 4l..4l+3 as float4, sum-of-squares via a 5-step
__shfl_xor butterfly, float4 normalize+SiLU write. One-thread-per-row
kept as fallback for D % 4 != 0.

Measured on beverin MI300A (nid003020, ROCm 6.3):
  old 170.7 us / 74 GB/s  ->  new 4.8 us / ~2600 GB/s (~49% of HBM roof), ~35x
  (batched 1000-launch event timing; rocprof per-launch avg 6.15 us)
Correctness: test_kda_correct 11/11 PASS (max_rel 1e-6); old-vs-new
outputs identical (max_abs_diff 3e-7). Docs updated (kda.md, reference row 16).

63b2ec3 test(issue-101): fix kda_delta device-template direct launch — pass worker/P runtime args
Same bug class as the #88 rope fix (pr-112): the device test launched
_t_kda_heads_batched without the leading worker/P runtime args, which
TypeErrors on any CUDA stack ('missing 2 required positional arguments:
K and V'). Launch with grid (1,), worker=0, P=1 — the task-striding loop
covers all (batch, head) tasks; the compiled path passes worker=pid,
P=grid. Verified on GB10 (sm_121): 20 passed, 1 skipped.

5316da6 refactor(capture): remove duplicated gdn_delta method (#136)
The union merge of #129 (Stage-2 DeepSeek megakernel, bb2374c) left two
byte-identical `def gdn_delta(` definitions in capture.py (lines 1254
and 1474). The second silently shadowed the first — harmless at runtime
but a confusing diff waiting to happen.

Removed the second copy (109 lines, 0 additions). Behavior unchanged:
the single surviving definition is byte-identical to the removed one
(verified via diff before deletion) and the module AST-parses clean.

Closes #135

## Register-prefetch plain prefill (issue #149) — 1.7x/2.2x on the two prefill rows, zero LDS

The plain kernel's prefill regime has the same serial key chain as decode,
but enough query blocks to fill the machine — the bound is per-warp
load→use latency, and the lever is in-flight depth per warp. Two variants
landed (issue #149), both behind the plain-forward dispatcher
(`launch_auto`, priority pf → staged → serial):

  * **Register-prefetch kernel `dsa_sparse_fwd_pf_kernel`** (default for
    prefill, `VK_DSA_PF=0/2` to force off/everywhere): width-specialized
    (`WT = main+tail` tiles compile-time; dynamic widths keep the serial
    kernel), it loads key `k+1`'s row + index into per-lane REGISTERS
    before the online-softmax update over key `k` consumes the
    register-held key `k` — 2 key rows in flight per warp with ZERO LDS
    and therefore no residency loss (full occupancy, unlike the #80-style
    LDS staging whose footprint caps blocks/CU). Per-key arithmetic is
    identical to the serial kernel (same ascending-d order, same
    reduction trees), so all correctness rows are bit-comparable.
  * **LDS-staged plain kernel `dsa_sparse_fwd_stage_kernel`** (opt-in
    `VK_DSA_STAGE=2`, kti via `VK_DSA_KTI`): the #80 double-buffer
    pattern applied to the plain path, gated to prefill. Measured LOSES
    at the wide shapes: at W=640/BQ=4 the kti=4 tile (41 KB) caps
    residency at 1 block/CU (3.6 ms vs 1.35 ms serial at DSv3 prefill);
    it only wins the GLM H=1 row at kti=2 (346.7 us) — which the pf
    kernel beats (272 us) without LDS. Kept for A/B only.

Measured (nid002766/nid003020, 2026-09-18, exclusive nodes, perf-level
high; two repeats, spread < 2%):

| shape | #51 baseline | serial+width-spec | pf-auto (shipped) | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM prefill H=1 (481.9 us / 1116 GB/s) | 481.9 | 388.6 | **272.2 us / 2019 GB/s** | **1.77x** |
| DSv3 prefill H=1 (1853 us / 1464 GB/s) | 1853.0 | 1366.3 | **841.6 us / 3184 GB/s** | **2.20x**, 62% of HBM roof |
| GLM serving prefill H=64 (new row) | — | 16852 | **12872 us / 2711 GB/s** | 1.31x vs serial |
| all decode + split rows | unchanged | identical | identical (±0.5%) | — |

Width specialization of the serial kernel alone (scratch-resident
accumulator removal) was worth 1.24–1.37x; the register pipeline adds
1.4–1.6x on top. The H=64 serving row (each of 64 heads re-reads the
same `topk` keys — 8x the DSv3-prefill traffic) lands at 51% of the
DRAM roof with the same code path; amortizing that re-read across heads
is the remaining structural lever and is out of scope here.

## The decode binding constraint is OCCUPANCY / key-stream latency, not HBM

  * **Decode grids are tiny**: the launcher is `grid(ceil(S_q/BQ), H)` —
    the GLM-5.3-Flash decode shape runs **64 blocks on 228 CUs** (one
    per head), DSv3 decode **16 blocks**. Each block streams its `topk`
    keys strictly serially (one key per lane iteration, no double-buffered
    key tile), so per-block latency ≈ `topk` serial L2 round-trips.
  * **Effective bandwidth confirms it**: 21.5 GB/s at the full-topk
    decode shape is 0.4% of the HBM roof — but the entire kv working set
    (`topk·W·2 B` = 1 MB at topk=2048) is L2-resident, and the measured
    rate is ~0.3% of MI300A's L2 bandwidth too. The kernel is bound by
    in-flight memory parallelism, not by any roof.
  * **Serving takeaway**: per layer, GLM-5.3-Flash decode paid 0.20 ms
    (topk=128) / 0.40 ms (topk=256) / 3.12 ms (full topk=2048) for the
    sparse forward vs 0.2–0.9 ms for the indexer stage (see
    [`../dsa-topk/gfx942.md`](../dsa-topk/gfx942.md)) — the forward
    dominated and scaled linearly with `topk`. The split-key path below
    removes this: 0.045 / 0.059 / 0.156 ms at the `split_for`
    recommendation, so the indexer is now the slower stage at full
    topk.
  * **Prefill is closer to the roof** (21–28% of HBM at S_q=8192): more
    query blocks hide the key-stream latency; AI 1.8–2.0 FLOP/B is
    ~125× below the ridge, so this kernel family is memory-shaped by
    construction (each selected key is used once per head — the
    H-fold kv re-read is the structural cost the tiled-key/persistent
    follow-on must amortize).
  * **The follow-on levers**, in expected impact order: (1) ~~split_kv for
    the forward~~ **DONE** — `dsa_sparse_fwd_split` + `split_for`, 20.0x
    at full topk (section above); (2) ~~double-buffered key tiles to
    overlap loads with the online-softmax update~~ **DONE (issue #149)**
    — register-resident prefetch on the plain prefill path, 1.77x/2.20x

7bf8d89 perf(mla_fwd): fused-head prefill — cross-head KV reuse + wide-rank register pipeline (issue #151)
The plain prefill grid re-reads the head-SHARED k_c/k_pe/v_c latent once
per (query tile, head) and its one-key-at-a-time loop is latency-bound
(~1300 cycles/key on MI300A). Two kernel-level changes close most of the
prefill gap:

* mla_fwd_headfused_kernel<BQ, BH>: a block owns BQ·BH (row, head) pairs
  (one wavefront each) all streaming the same key sequence, so the latent
  is read once per (query tile, head group) instead of once per (query
  tile, head) — a BH-fold traffic cut absorbed by L1. Heads per block =
  min(H, 16/BQ) rounded to a power of two (mla_prefill_heads_per_block);
  BQ=4 remains the prefill query tile.
* mla_fwd_headfused_wide_kernel<BQ, BH, LP> for wide ranks (kv_lora_rank
  = 512, K3): consecutive-lane float4 row slices (2 loads per row instead
  of 8 strided scalars), a BN=2-key register pipeline (a tile's k_c/k_pe/
  v_c loads issue up front so the score→expf→accumulate chain runs
  ALU-only), and an online-softmax fast path that skips the accumulator
  rescale when a key does not advance the running max (one expf per key).

Two measured dead ends are documented in docs/kernels/mla.md: an
LDS-staged double-buffered BN-key tile variant spills ~57 SGPRs on gfx942

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background, provider, or detached work that has no native completion notification, then return.

Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively when they complete or need attention. In an interactive chat, return control instead of calling this merely to wait. Use this tool for provider jobs, remembered detached foreground runs, or other background work without a native notification path. Headless runs auto-drain current-session subagent work at agent_end; use this tool only when the current turn must receive non-notifying background work results.

• { } — return when the first initially active async run or registered provider item finishes, or when a subagent needs attention.
• { all: true } — wait for every async run, provider item, and remembered detached foreground descendant that was active when the call began.
• { id: "..." } — wait for one async or remembered detached foreground subagent run (id or prefix). Named async runs that already finished return their terminal result references.
• { id: "...", nonBlocking: true } — resolve the prefix once, persist an exact-run wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this for detached work without native completion delivery; the originating interactive session wakes on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout.
• { stopOnAttention: false } — for blocking waits only, keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.
• { timeoutMs: 600000 } — stop waiting after N ms; active work keeps running. Omitted values use waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 minutes. Window expiry returns a non-error window_elapsed result with active work identities.

Non-blocking subscriptions are visible in subagent status and differ from disabling waitTool: waitTool.enabled=false returns immediately without registering any future wake. Provider jobs are session-scoped and identified exactly, so replacing one job with another cannot hide a completion. Provider extensions must be explicitly loaded in this process. In a child agent, keep `bg_wait` in the child tool allowlist and load each provider through the agent's extensions or subagentOnlyExtensions; this tool never loads providers or grants tools itself.

id.description: Async run or remembered detached foreground run id/prefix to wait for one specific run. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use bg_wait for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, or when same-turn blocking results are truly needed. Omit to wait across every active async run started in this session only when a same-turn wait is truly needed.

nonBlocking.description: When true, resolve id to one exact run, persist a wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this only for provider, detached, or other background work without a native completion notification; ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively and do not need a subscription. The originating session is woken on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout. Requires id and cannot be combined with all.

all.description: Wait for ALL active runs to finish. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use all only when a same-turn result from tracked background work is truly needed. Default false: return when the first tracked run or provider item finishes or needs attention. Ignored when id targets a single run.

timeoutMs.description: Give up waiting after this many milliseconds (the runs keep going regardless). Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use a wait timeout only when same-turn results are truly needed for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification. Defaults to config waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 1800000 (30 minutes). Window expiry is a non-error active-work result.

stopOnAttention.description: For a blocking wait that is truly needed, stop when a run needs attention by default. Set false to keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.

# MI300A Validation & Performance Report — Consolidated `main` (5eb2e29)

## 1. Consolidation integrity — CONFIRMED

All 8 fix branches merged cleanly into `main`; merge-fidelity was verified three independent ways:
- Source-identity diffs of each branch tip's kernel files vs HEAD (only legitimate post-merge evolution differs)
- Merge-commit graph audit (`88b0486` #150, `edab4dc` #147, etc.)
- **Binary-level A/B**: rebuilt branch tips (e4e590c / cfd8be8 / 3c76e4a) and merged lib side-by-side on the same node — **bit-identical outputs and timings**

## 2. Correctness — 100% PASS (jobs 649120, 649126)

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| #144 kda (delta-rule fwd, layer_norm_gated, gate_chunk_cumsum, determinism) | **PASS, 0 failures** |
| #147 mhc (fp64-reference gate: 5 seeds × NSLICE 1–256 × 3 shapes) | **187/187 GATE PASS** |
| #149 dsa (decode/short/prefill, DSv3 tail>0, split+combine) | **PASS, 0 failures** |
| #151 mla (40/40 incl. fused-head prefill + BQ=4) | **PASS** |
| #145 moe_aux (16/16, bit-exact quant/sort) | **PASS** |
| #146 gemm_bf16 (incl. split-K sweep) | **PASS** |
| #150 moe prefill V5 (shipped default, small+big-shape) | **PASS** |
| #152 cross-node KV striped (host unit tests) | **20/20 PASS** |
| #150 **V6 opt-in** (`VK_MOE_PF_VARIANT=6`) | **Faults** — ⚠️ pre-existing: the branch itself documented "ANY V6 launch faults with HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_APERTURE_VIOLATION... blocked until root-caused." Merged main reproduces the documented state exactly (V6 big-shape actually passes; small-shape + bench fault). **Not a consolidation regression.** |

## 3. Performance — kernel-level verification vs branch evidence

The bench-table rows for µs-scale kernels are **unreliable** (per-iteration event-pair harness floors + the documented ROCm 6.3 0.0-quirk at DVFS transitions + at least one slow node session). I therefore verified the actual claims with **batched 1000-launch event-pair timing + output checksums** against the branch-tip libs:

| Claim | Branch tip | Merged main | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| #144 kda layer_norm_gated N=8192 D=128 = 4.8µs | 4.69–4.95µs | **4.73–4.88µs**, identical checksum (429.672) | ✅ reproduced |
| #144 gate_chunk_cumsum ≈ 5.7–10.5µs | 10.52µs | **10.52µs**, identical checksum | ✅ reproduced |
| #147 mhc_pre ns=32 (GLM decode n=1) = 30.8–31.4µs | 27.37µs | **27.34µs**, same checksum | ✅ reproduced |
| #147 strict chain (ns=1) ≈ 816µs | 812µs | 812µs (via #147-tip parity) | ✅ |
| #150 prefill V5 M=1024 = 638.5µs / 20.2 TF | — | **617.0µs / 20.9 TF (2.68x)** | ✅ matches |
| #145 moe_aux scatter_reduce ≈ L2 roof | — | **2773–2905 GB/s = 94–99% of the 2936 GB/s L2 roof** | ✅ |
| #146 gemm splitk K=7168 serving shapes | — | **63.9–97.4µs, up to 1236 GB/s** | ✅ healthy |

Also confirmed empirically: `setperflevel` is sudo-gated on every node tested (nid002696/27766), idle sclk 95–96 MHz, mclk 1300 MHz fixed, boost reaches **~2100 MHz** after ~8s of sustained load and decays in ~2s — matching the docs' own methodology notes.

## 4. Caveats for reading the bench logs

- `vk-val-attn-649120.out` / `vk-val-moe-649126.out` / `vk-val-warm-649216.out` bench **tables** for kda/mhc/dsa/mla small-kernel rows (e.g. "236.7µs layer_norm", "1118µs mhc ns=32", "65ms dsa decode") are harness/session artifacts — the kernel-level A/B proves the real numbers are the branch-evidence values. Use the docs' guidance: absolute µs from per-launch harnesses are upper bounds; ratios/scalings are the robust signal.
- One probe session (job 649227, nid002426) measured *all* libs — including branch-era code — systematically 36–50x slow; a node/session state issue, not code (disproven by the clean three-lib A/B, job 649339).
- dsa/mla absolute rows carry the same caveat; their relative sweeps (split-scaling 15.5x @ split=32, BQ ladders) match expected behavior. Kernel-level A/B for those two would be the natural follow-up if you want the same rigor applied there.

**Bottom line: consolidated `main` is validated on MI300A — all correctness gates pass, the perf-critical paths reproduce their branch evidence bit-for-bit, and the only known fault (#150 V6) is the branch's own documented, still-unsafe opt-in.**

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background, provider, or detached work that has no native completion notification, then return.

Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively when they complete or need attention. In an interactive chat, return control instead of calling this merely to wait. Use this tool for provider jobs, remembered detached foreground runs, or other background work without a native notification path. Headless runs auto-drain current-session subagent work at agent_end; use this tool only when the current turn must receive non-notifying background work results.

• { } — return when the first initially active async run or registered provider item finishes, or when a subagent needs attention.
• { all: true } — wait for every async run, provider item, and remembered detached foreground descendant that was active when the call began.
• { id: "..." } — wait for one async or remembered detached foreground subagent run (id or prefix). Named async runs that already finished return their terminal result references.
• { id: "...", nonBlocking: true } — resolve the prefix once, persist an exact-run wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this for detached work without native completion delivery; the originating interactive session wakes on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout.
• { stopOnAttention: false } — for blocking waits only, keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.
• { timeoutMs: 600000 } — stop waiting after N ms; active work keeps running. Omitted values use waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 minutes. Window expiry returns a non-error window_elapsed result with active work identities.

Non-blocking subscriptions are visible in subagent status and differ from disabling waitTool: waitTool.enabled=false returns immediately without registering any future wake. Provider jobs are session-scoped and identified exactly, so replacing one job with another cannot hide a completion. Provider extensions must be explicitly loaded in this process. In a child agent, keep `bg_wait` in the child tool allowlist and load each provider through the agent's extensions or subagentOnlyExtensions; this tool never loads providers or grants tools itself.

id.description: Async run or remembered detached foreground run id/prefix to wait for one specific run. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use bg_wait for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, or when same-turn blocking results are truly needed. Omit to wait across every active async run started in this session only when a same-turn wait is truly needed.

nonBlocking.description: When true, resolve id to one exact run, persist a wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this only for provider, detached, or other background work without a native completion notification; ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively and do not need a subscription. The originating session is woken on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout. Requires id and cannot be combined with all.

all.description: Wait for ALL active runs to finish. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use all only when a same-turn result from tracked background work is truly needed. Default false: return when the first tracked run or provider item finishes or needs attention. Ignored when id targets a single run.

timeoutMs.description: Give up waiting after this many milliseconds (the runs keep going regardless). Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use a wait timeout only when same-turn results are truly needed for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification. Defaults to config waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 1800000 (30 minutes). Window expiry is a non-error active-work result.

stopOnAttention.description: For a blocking wait that is truly needed, stop when a run needs attention by default. Set false to keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.

## Problem

`dsa_sparse_fwd` **decode** is the single largest performance bottleneck in the stack — 3–4 orders of magnitude off both rooflines, and latency-bound rather than throughput-bound.

Post-consolidation MI300A validation (2026-09-23, beverin; kernel-level batched-timing verification):

| decode shape (H=64, S_q=1, dim=256, tail=0) | time | rate | vs roof |
|---|---|---|---|
| topk=2048 (full topk) | **3.125 ms** | ~43 GFLOP/s, <1 GB/s | ~0.003% of 1307 TF bf16 |
| topk=256 (serving) | **397 µs** | ~42 GFLOP/s, ~21 GB/s | ~0.4% of 5.3 TB/s HBM |
| topk=128 (serving) | **203 µs** | ~41 GFLOP/s | same |

## Diagnosis

* TFLOP/s is **flat (~42) across topk = 128 → 2048** and the BQ autotuner sweep is **flat (BQ=1..8)** ⇒ neither more KV nor more queries helps. Not memory-bound (AI≈2 at ~21 GB/s), not compute-bound: **latency-bound on the per-token serial chain** (score → topk → gather → attend) with only ~64 CTAs of parallelism.
* It dominates the decode layer budget: ~397 µs/layer (serving topk=256) vs ~270 µs for all three MoE GEMVs combined and ~50–100 µs for kda+mhc+mla state ops.

## Proposal

Parallelize **within** the token, mirroring #149's split+combine pattern (already in main for the KV-dim path) but applied to the token-serial chain:

1. **Block-per-KV-chunk partials + tiny combine**: each selected-kv chunk gets its own CTA computing a partial softmax/accumulator; a second small kernel combines. Removes the single-CTA-per-head serial walk.
2. **Fuse indexer score+topk into the gather** where the topk indices are produced on-device, removing the round-trip.
3. Consider persistent CTAs / programmatic dependent launch to hide the combine.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decode topk=256 serving shape: **≥4x** vs 397 µs (target ≤100 µs), no regression at topk=128/2048
- [ ] Existing dsa oracle tests: 0 failures (decode/short/prefill, incl. DSv3 tail>0)
- [ ] Measured with **batched ≥1000-launch event-pair timing + output checksums** on MI300A (see methodology note below)
- [ ] Raw bench log + doc table update in `docs/performance/dsa/gfx942.md`

## Measurement methodology (mandatory on beverin)

Per-iteration event-pair benches floor at ~230 µs for µs-scale kernels and ROCm 6.3 emits 0.0 µs readings at DVFS transitions; `setperflevel` is sudo-gated (idle sclk 95 MHz, boost ~2100 MHz, ~8 s ramp). Batch 1000 launches inside one event pair, ≥4 batches, checksum outputs, warm up ~15 s before first measurement. Reference: validation session logs `/capstor/scratch/cscs/xyao/vk-val-attn-649120.out`, docs/performance/dsa/gfx942.md.
EOF
cat > /tmp/issue-moe-fp8.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

MoE **decode** expert GEMVs stream expert weights at ~20–23% of the HBM roof — ~4–5x headroom left on the table, worth roughly ~200 µs/layer at batch 1.

Post-consolidation MI300A validation (2026-09-23, beverin), split-K decode rows (bf16):

| shape (M=5) | best cfg | time | GB/s | % of 5.3 TB/s roof |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N=6288 K=7168 | splitk=8 | 95.3 µs | 1236 | 23% |
| N=3584 K=7168 | splitk=8 | 63.4 µs | 1074 | 20% |
| N=896 K=7168 | splitk=8 | 50.0 µs | 329 | 6% (latency-floored) |

Per decode layer: 3 GEMVs ≈ 270 µs at batch 1 (vs ~397 µs dsa decode — see companion issue).

**Out of scope (already near-optimal):** prefill V5 at M=1024 runs at AI ≈ 258 FLOP/B (ridge 247) and ~85% of memory roof. Do not spend time there without cross-token expert reuse.

## Proposal

1. **bf16 path**: wider vectorized loads / TMA-style staging on the weight stream; L2 residency for hot experts (repeat-expert locality at batch>1). Target ≥3.5 TB/s (≥65% roof) on the N=6288/3584 shapes.
2. **FP8 path**: halves weight bytes → doubles the bandwidth ceiling for the same shapes. Starting point: preserved WIP `89a3a35` ("wip(issue-148): … fp8 gemv benches/probes") — extract the probes from that commit rather than starting fresh.

- [ ] Raw bench log + doc update in `docs/performance/moe-fused/gfx942.md`

- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- If kb_show_binding reports no project is bound, ask the user to run /ada:bind before any other knowledge-base operation.
- Use kb_list_projects to discover knowledge-base projects when the repo is not bound or the user references one by name.
- Use kb_list_documents to enumerate notes in the bound project when the user asks what has been recorded or you need to find a slug.
- Use kb_get_document to read an existing note by slug or id before answering questions grounded in the knowledge base.
- Use kb_upsert_document to save a decision, summary, or note to the knowledge base. Provide a slug, a title (required when creating), and markdown content that may use [[slug]] wikilinks to other notes.
- Use kb_backlinks before renaming or deleting a note to see which other notes link to it via [[slug]], and to confirm the target exists.
- Use kb_resolve_links to show what a note links to and confirm those targets exist; dangling [[slug]] links are flagged, not errors.
- Do not invoke subagents unless the operator requested delegation directly or through applicable instructions.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: kb_show_binding
toolsAdded.description: Show which Ada AI knowledge-base project this repository is bound to, by reading .pi/kb-binding.json (no network). Call this first to learn which project knowledge-base operations target, and to detect when the repo is not bound.

toolsAdded.name: kb_list_projects
toolsAdded.description: List the Ada AI knowledge-base projects available to the current session (id and name for each). Use when the repo is not bound and you need to suggest a project, or when the user asks what knowledge bases exist.

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_list_documents
toolsAdded.description: List documents in a knowledge-base project as metadata (id, slug, title, updated) — bodies are NOT included and there is no full-text search in v1, so call kb_get_document to read a specific note. Uses the repo binding unless project_id is given.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_get_document
toolsAdded.description: Fetch one knowledge-base document WITH its markdown content, by slug (unique within a project) or numeric id. Use to read a note the user references or one found by kb_list_documents or a link graph.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_upsert_document
toolsAdded.description: Create or update a knowledge-base note by slug. Creates when the slug is new (title required) and updates the existing document in place when it exists (omitted fields are left unchanged server-side). Content may use [[slug]] wikilinks to other notes in the same project.

slug.description: Note slug: 1-80 lowercase [a-z0-9-], not starting or ending with '-'.

title.description: Note title. Required when creating; left unchanged on update when omitted.

content.description: Markdown body. May contain [[slug]] wikilinks. Omit on update to leave unchanged. Capped at 1 MB.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_backlinks
toolsAdded.description: Compute which documents in a knowledge-base project reference a slug via [[slug]] wikilinks, and whether the target document itself exists. The server does not compute backlinks, so this scans all documents in the project. Use before renaming or deleting a note, or to understand its impact.

slug.description: Target slug to find backlinks for.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: kb_resolve_links
toolsAdded.description: Resolve one hop of outbound [[slug]] links from a note, fetching each target. Dangling links (target document does not exist) are flagged, not treated as errors. Use to show what a note links to and verify its targets.

slug.description: Slug of the note to resolve outbound links from.

project_id.description: Knowledge-base project id. Defaults to this repo's binding (.pi/kb-binding.json).

organization_id.description: Organization id scope. Defaults to the binding or personal scope.

toolsAdded.name: vcc_recall
toolsAdded.description: Search session history. Defaults to active lineage; use scope:'all' to include off-lineage branches. Supports regex queries, paging, and expand indices. Use scope:'compaction:N' to search within a specific compaction's message range.

query.description: Search terms or regex pattern (e.g. 'hook|inject', 'fail.*build'). Multi-word = OR ranked by relevance.

expand.description: Entry indices to return full untruncated content for. Works alone (any index in scope) or alongside query (expands matching entries on the current page).

page.description: Page number (1-based) for paginated search results. Default: 1.

scope.description: Search scope. Options: 'lineage' (default), 'all' (entire session), 'compaction:N' (within compaction #N), 'compaction:latest' (most recent compaction segment).

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background, provider, or detached work that has no native completion notification, then return.

Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively when they complete or need attention. In an interactive chat, return control instead of calling this merely to wait. Use this tool for provider jobs, remembered detached foreground runs, or other background work without a native notification path. Headless runs auto-drain current-session subagent work at agent_end; use this tool only when the current turn must receive non-notifying background work results.

• { } — return when the first initially active async run or registered provider item finishes, or when a subagent needs attention.
• { all: true } — wait for every async run, provider item, and remembered detached foreground descendant that was active when the call began.
• { id: "..." } — wait for one async or remembered detached foreground subagent run (id or prefix). Named async runs that already finished return their terminal result references.
• { id: "...", nonBlocking: true } — resolve the prefix once, persist an exact-run wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this for detached work without native completion delivery; the originating interactive session wakes on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout.
• { stopOnAttention: false } — for blocking waits only, keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.
• { timeoutMs: 600000 } — stop waiting after N ms; active work keeps running. Omitted values use waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 minutes. Window expiry returns a non-error window_elapsed result with active work identities.

Non-blocking subscriptions are visible in subagent status and differ from disabling waitTool: waitTool.enabled=false returns immediately without registering any future wake. Provider jobs are session-scoped and identified exactly, so replacing one job with another cannot hide a completion. Provider extensions must be explicitly loaded in this process. In a child agent, keep `bg_wait` in the child tool allowlist and load each provider through the agent's extensions or subagentOnlyExtensions; this tool never loads providers or grants tools itself.

id.description: Async run or remembered detached foreground run id/prefix to wait for one specific run. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use bg_wait for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, or when same-turn blocking results are truly needed. Omit to wait across every active async run started in this session only when a same-turn wait is truly needed.

nonBlocking.description: When true, resolve id to one exact run, persist a wake subscription, and return immediately. Use this only for provider, detached, or other background work without a native completion notification; ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively and do not need a subscription. The originating session is woken on completion, failure, attention, reconciliation failure, or timeout. Requires id and cannot be combined with all.

all.description: Wait for ALL active runs to finish. Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use all only when a same-turn result from tracked background work is truly needed. Default false: return when the first tracked run or provider item finishes or needs attention. Ignored when id targets a single run.

timeoutMs.description: Give up waiting after this many milliseconds (the runs keep going regardless). Ordinary async subagent runs already notify this session natively; use a wait timeout only when same-turn results are truly needed for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification. Defaults to config waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 1800000 (30 minutes). Window expiry is a non-error active-work result.

stopOnAttention.description: For a blocking wait that is truly needed, stop when a run needs attention by default. Set false to keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention; supervisor/contact requests still stop the wait.

toolsAdded.name: subagents_enable
toolsAdded.description: Enable pi-subagents delegation and management tools without launching work. Call when delegation is authorized by the current request or applicable user/project instructions, or when managing existing runs. Direct execution is the default; complexity alone never authorizes delegation. Full tools are available on the next model request.

toolsAdded.name: goal_complete
toolsAdded.description: Mark an active /goal complete only when the latest effective Goal contract explicitly says Goal mode is active, supplies the matching current goal_id, and every requirement is verified. Tool visibility alone does not activate Goal mode. Never call for ordinary work, partial progress, blockers, failures, or unverified work.

goal_id.description: The exact goal_id shown in the current active /goal prompt. Used only to reject stale completion calls from older turns.

summary.description: State what was completed and what evidence verified it. Do not use this tool to report partial progress, blockers, failures, or remaining work.

toolsAdded.name: goal_blocked
toolsAdded.description: Stop an active /goal only when the latest effective Goal contract explicitly says Goal mode is active, supplies the matching current goal_id, and the same evidenced external blocker recurred for at least three consecutive Goal turns. Tool visibility alone does not activate Goal mode. Never call for ordinary clarification, uncertainty, incomplete work, or recoverable failures.

goal_id.description: The exact goal_id shown in the current active /goal prompt.

reason.description: The specific user or external action required to unblock the goal.

evidence.description: Concrete evidence from the repeated attempts that proves the impasse.

repeated_turns.description: Number of separate turns spent trying to resolve this same blocker.

toolsAdded.name: goal_wait
toolsAdded.description: Keep an active /goal quiet only when the latest effective Goal contract explicitly says Goal mode is active, supplies the matching current goal_id, and progress depends on an arranged external wake event or one safety deadline. Tool visibility alone does not activate Goal mode. Call goal_wait alone. Requests below 10000ms are clamped to 10000ms. Never call for ordinary unfinished work.

goal_id.description: The exact goal_id shown in the current active /goal prompt.

reason.description: Why the goal is waiting and which external event should wake it.

resume_after_ms.description: Optional safety deadline in milliseconds that requests one continuation if no wake message arrives. Values below 10000 are accepted but clamped to 10000.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_supervisor
toolsAdded.description: Native pi-subagents supervisor channel. Use reply/pending/status to answer child subagent requests without overriding pi-intercom.

toolsAdded.name: subagent
toolsAdded.description:
Delegate one child with {agent,task?}; otherwise choose exactly one of {workflowScript,args?}, {workflowScriptPath,args?} or {workflow,args}. agent/task exclude workflow inputs; task excludes action. agent may target management actions. action is management/control; validate accepts either script without launching. workflowScriptPath loads from request cwd before sandbox execution.
Scripts: JavaScript statement bodies with explicit return, top-level await, plain helpers/Promise chains; nested async function/arrow/method helpers are rejected. Await runs.run('key',{agent,task}) before .output; await runs.all([{key,agent,task},...]) for an ordered array, not a key map. Observe every stored run promise with direct await, Promise.race or Promise.all. mode.description: steer delivery mode; worktree.cleanup supports plan only, no apply/removal.

steeringRecovery.description: steer: pause/revive after missed acknowledgment; default true in direct steer mode, forced false by extension RPC for exact ownership.

additional.description: grant-spawn-budget: root interactive parent + native user confirmation only; total grants capped at original configured cap.

scope.description: watchdog.configure scope; default session, persistent only if explicit.

mission.description: false disables; true invalid. Object: exactly one non-empty title or summary; objective/labels optional; goal only true, requires budget.tokens.

config.description: create/update agent config; object or JSON string.

args.description: Bounded plain-JSON args for named, inline, or file-backed workflows; raw-script args are exposed deeply frozen and persisted, so do not include secrets.

workflowScript.description: Inline JavaScript statement body; raw/unknown provenance, no runs.host. Use explicit return and top-level await; see tool guidance/guide workflows.

workflowScriptPath.description: Raw script file; host reads from request cwd before sandbox. Mutually exclusive with workflowScript and workflow.

preflight.description: Display-only lane hints; coverage mismatches warn, never change authority/execution.

chatProgress.description: auto: live card only for watched foreground in same Git repository. live-card requires same-repo async:false; async: omit or auto/off.

isolation.description: Shared cwd or managed git worktrees.

worktree.description: Isolate each workflow child in a managed git worktree; child worktree:false overrides default.

lane.description: Display/triage only; sourceRef is opaque, never resolved by status.

context.description: fresh/fork overrides every child; profile requires agent's declared defaultContext, ignoring config. Omitted: defaultSubagentContext wins over each agent defaultContext; implicit fork needs persisted parent + leaf, else fresh. forkContext may prune forks before spawn.

async.description: Background; default asyncByDefault. false only to block parent.

timeoutMs.description: Timeout. Foreground and single async runs use config timeoutMs, else 30m; async composites have no default parent deadline. Alias maxRuntimeMs.

checkpointBeforeDeadlineMs.description: Async single-agent runs only: the runner requests that the child checkpoint and stop this many ms before the run deadline (best-effort; the deadline kill still applies).

toolBudget.description: soft nudges; after hard, block tools (default read/grep/find/ls, '*' for all) so child can finalize.

usageBudget.description: Root-only reported usage; hard prevents later launches. Running children are not stopped.

machine.description: Herdr saved machine id or label; runs an external CLI agent there. cwd then means the directory on that machine.

share.description: Upload session to GitHub Gist; default false.

sessionDir.description: Session log directory; default temp, independent of share.

output.description: Child output path or false; relative workflow paths use managed artifact routing. Bind durable output here, not task prose; return outputReference/outputPathMapping/artifactPaths.

outputMode.description: Default inline; file-only requires output path.

skill.description: Skills: names/CSV/array; false disables, true uses default.

model.description: Child model provider/id; bare id only if unique. Suffix :off/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max overrides agent thinking default.

fast.description: Native OpenAI-Codex priority tier; default false, may cost more/quota.

outputSchema.description: Structured output schema override; false disables an agent default.

agentContract.description: Compatibility behavior. Omit for the default behavior.

acceptance.description: Evidence policy; omit for read-only/review. false disables; true invalid. Prefer object; see guide tool-reference for levels, evidence and review.required.

gate.description: Host gate command run after the child finishes: a string, or { command, output: "json", schema?, timeoutMs? } whose passing stdout becomes structuredOutput (not with outputSchema). Cannot be combined with acceptance; an explicit acceptance of false is treated as omitted.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Line-coverage gate for the host (CPU reference) build.

Runs ``gcov`` over every ``.gcno`` produced by a coverage build, merges the
results per source file (so headers included from several translation units
are counted once), and reports per-file and total line coverage. Exits
non-zero when coverage falls below ``--min`` (default 100) for any source
file under ``--source-dir`` (default src/c/).

Branch coverage is computed and reported for information but, unless
``--require-branches`` is set, it does not fail the gate.

Lines whose source carries a ``LCOV_EXCL_LINE`` comment are intentionally
excluded from the gate (used for defensively-dead branches such as malloc
failure handling that a test cannot deterministically trigger). gcov's ``-b``
mode appends ``*`` to the count on lines with an unexecuted branch; that
suffix is ignored so such lines still count as covered.

Example:
    python3 scripts/coverage.py --build-dir build/coverage --source-dir src/c --min 100
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

_SOURCE_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*([^:]+):\s*(\d+):(.*)$")
_SOURCE_HDR = re.compile(r"^\s*-:\s*0:Source:(.+)$")
_BRANCH_HDR = re.compile(r"^\s*branch\s+\d+\s+(taken|never executed)")
_NUMERIC = re.compile(r"^\d+$")


@dataclass
class FileStats:
    executable: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
    covered: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
    branches_total = 0
    branches_taken = 0

    def add_exec(self, ln: int) -> None:
        self.executable.add(ln)

    def add_covered(self, ln: int) -> None:
        self.covered.add(ln)
        self.executable.add(ln)

    @property
    def total(self) -> int:
        return len(self.executable)

    @property
    def hit(self) -> int:
        return len(self.covered & self.executable)
